statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r equals the integer represented by s under the standard Roman rule: r = sum_{i=0}^{len(s)-1} c_i, where c_i = -v(s[i]) if i+1 < len(s) and v(s[i]) < v(s[i+1]), and c_i = v(s[i]) otherwise; v is defined by v('I')=1, v('V')=5, v('X')=10, v('L')=50, v('C')=100, v('D')=500, v('M')=1000.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 15; every byte s[i] with 0 <= i < len(s) is the ASCII code of one of 'I','V','X','L','C','D','M'; and s is a valid standard Roman numeral in [1,3999] (canonical representation, allowing only the usual additive forms and the six subtractive pairs IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, CM).

statement: For every s satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r and does not fail (no panic, overflow, out-of-bounds access, or other failure).
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 15; every byte s[i] with 0 <= i < len(s) is the ASCII code of one of 'I','V','X','L','C','D','M'; and s is a valid standard Roman numeral in [1,3999] (canonical representation, allowing only the usual additive forms and the six subtractive pairs IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, CM).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every j with 0 <= j <= len(s), let p_j be the value of the prefix s[0..j) computed by the same sign rule: p_0 = 0; for j > 0, p_j = sum_{i=0}^{j-1} d_i where d_i = -v(s[i]) if i+1 < j and v(s[i]) < v(s[i+1]), and d_i = v(s[i]) otherwise; v('I')=1, v('V')=5, v('X')=10, v('L')=50, v('C')=100, v('D')=500, v('M')=1000. statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if s = u ++ v for byte slices u and v (possibly empty) such that every symbol of u has value at least every symbol of v, i.e. for all i < len(u) and j < len(v), v(u[i]) >= v(v[j]), then r = value(u) + value(v), where value(t) is the sign-sum value of t defined as sum_{i=0}^{len(t)-1} c_i with c_i = -v(t[i]) if i+1 < len(t) and v(t[i]) < v(t[i+1]), and c_i = v(t[i]) otherwise; v('I')=1, v('V')=5, v('X')=10, v('L')=50, v('C')=100, v('D')=500, v('M')=1000, and value(empty)=0.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 15; every byte s[i] with 0 <= i < len(s) is the ASCII code of one of 'I','V','X','L','C','D','M'; and s is a valid standard Roman numeral in [1,3999] (canonical representation, allowing only the usual additive forms and the six subtractive pairs IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, CM).
